title: Tenanted KV schema mismatch during on-prem upgrade: surgical hotpatch and customer escalation runbook
creator: Riya Patel
description:
Summary: During a staged private (on-prem/VPC) operator upgrade to private-operator-2.1.4, a subset of tenants experienced reconciliation failures caused by a latent KV cache schema change introduced in the runtime build. The operator's CRD migration path did not detect tenant-specific prefix encoding changes, producing a schema mismatch that caused KV reads to return nil for cache headers. Impacted tenants saw sustained controller reconcile errors, increased pod churn, and degraded inference latency for short-lived sessions. This ticket tracks the emergency investigation, a minimal surgical hotpatch, coordinated rollout, and post-release remediation steps.

Root cause hypothesis: a change to internal KV prefix encoding (added trailing metadata byte for forward compatibility) was deployed in runtime v1.18. Operator upgrade logic assumed idempotent read semantics; it attempted a migration only when a cluster-level marker was present. For tenants created before the marker, the operator attempted to reconcile with the new reader and silently dropped unrecognized cache entries, leaving tenants with empty prefix index and causing repeated rehydration storms.

Why this is urgent: Multiple customers (three enterprise tenants) escalated to SEs and opened high-severity support cases. Two customers reported request latencies >3x and pods restarting during reconcile loops. With Dedicated/Private customers, SLAs and scheduled maintenance expectations require a surgical fix with a non-invasive rollback plan.

Progress log and timeline: - 2025-02-18 09:12 UTC: PagerDuty P1 triggered by SE; initial triage shows recurring reconcile errors in operator logs with "kv: invalid prefix hdr". - 2025-02-18 12:40 UTC: Repro harness created against a snapshot of an affected tenant's namespace; local replay reproduces null-cache index. - 2025-02-19 03:00 UTC: Core suspect identified (prefix encoding change) and PoC shim implemented to attempt dual-mode reads. - 2025-02-20 10:30 UTC: Security and product on-call briefed; design for surgical hotpatch drafted. - 2025-02-22 16:00 UTC: Hotpatch branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/private-operator/pulls/3127 (see artifacts). - 2025-02-24 02:15 UTC: Limited canary deployment to two affected tenants in staging; observed successful reconciliation and stable pod counts. - 2025-02-26 21:00 UTC: Customer-facing runbook and rollback plan reviewed with Solutions (PR feedback incorporated). Current status: hotpatch awaiting final ops approval and CNC (customer notice) window scheduling.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpatch builds and passes full operator e2e w/ KV read dual-mode enabled
Canary patch deployed to 3 staging tenants for 48h with no reconcile errors
Rollback plan validated: helm rollback path restores previous operator image without data loss
Customer-facing CPS (communication) approved and two affected customers confirm improved latency metrics
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Take a snapshot of a pre-2.1 operator tenant namespace with KV entries encoded with v1 prefix format
2. Upgrade operator image to private-operator-2.1.4 without migration marker set
3. Observe operator logs for repeated reconcile errors: "kv: invalid prefix hdr" and 5xx controller events
4. Note that KV read returns nil for prefix index and the controller triggers cache rehydration storms
proposed_fix: Introduce a dual-mode KV reader in the operator that attempts existing read, falls back to legacy prefix decoding if primary parse fails
Add an upgrade-time safe migration job that converts legacy prefixes to normalized form incrementally per-tenant with idempotent checkpoints
Expose a tenant-scoped telemetry flag to detect how many keys required legacy fallback for monitoring and future opt-in migration
rollback_plan: 1. If hotpatch causes regressions, use helm rollback to previous operator revision (helm history/rollback <release> <rev>)
2. The previous operator image retains legacy reader; verify KV reads succeed and reconcile errors stop
3. If helm rollback fails, perform controlled pod eviction on operator daemonset and re-deploy previous image via kubectl apply
4. Notify customers of rollback and record for postmortem
validation_checks: Controller reconcile error count (Grafana dashboard private-operator /reconciles/errors) decreases to baseline within 15m of deploy
Pod restart rate for tenant namespaces returns to <1 restart/hour
Token-level latency at proxy edge for affected tenants improves to pre-upgrade baseline within 30m
Migration telemetry shows <1% of keys requiring fallback after 48h canary
review_feedback: PM (Jules Nguyen): prefer dual-mode reader as short-term mitigation; migration job should be opt-in per tenant
Security (Aisha Karim): confirm no sensitive payload deserialization occurs during fallback path; add unit tests for header parsing
Infra lead (Marco Ruiz): require canary to run 48h and network e2e to verify no latency amplification
Solutions eng (Lena Ortiz): include a small customer-facing script to collect operator logs and KV header stats for field triage
deployment_plan: 1. Build and sign hotpatch image: private-operator:2.1.4-hotpatch-20250226
2. Run CI e2e and static analyzer + security unit tests (expected time: 90m)
3. Canary rollout to 2 affected staging tenants during low-traffic window (02:00-04:00 UTC), monitor 48h
4. If canary green, coordinate phased rollout to production tenants in maintenance windows (max 3 tenants per window)
5. Post-deploy telemetry check and customer confirmation step
postmortem_actions: 1. Backfill operator preflight to detect KV prefix entropy changes before image promotion
2. Add automated migration marker and a one-click migration job in Console for Private customers
3. Improve release notes to highlight on-prem preflight expectations and possible data schema flags
4. Create a small e2e test matrix that simulates heterogeneous tenant histories for future upgrades
communications: Draft CNC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OnpremCNC - to be sent after canary confirms
Customer liaison email templates prepared for CS team; SEs briefed and ready for live handoffs
Weekly status update to executive TPM and account owners until fully remediated
notes: Trade-offs considered: performing broad migration proactively risks long-running jobs and increased IOPS on tenant stores. Chosen approach is conservative: dual-mode reader + opt-in incremental migration.
Longer-term: standardize KV header versioning and add forward/backward compatibility contracts in runtime spec v2
Next steps assigned: Ethan to land PR and verify canary; Riya to coordinate customer comms and schedule maintenance windows
